item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings Verstappen in control despite lead changes "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. item.title: Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings
item.description: Max Verstappen said George Russell's lock-up was "karma" for his comments about the Dutchman earlier in the Las Vegas weekend [Getty Images] Max Verstappen sealed his fourth win of the season with a stunning victory at a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. George Russell, who started second, locked up late on attempting a move on Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and finished ninth, while Charles Leclerc was given a 10-second time penalty for making contact with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Vegas. Max Verstappen - 10/10 An extraordinary display of racecraft. Inherited pole after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty and spent virtually the entire race being attacked, passed and then finding a way back through, while also working out the optimum energy deployment from inside his Red Bull. One of his finest victories. Lando Norris - 9/10 A remarkable recovery after dropping as low as 11th in the madness of the opening part of the race. Had genuine pace throughout and fought all the way back to second, finishing less than a second behind Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 9.5/10 One of the drives of the race. Qualified seventh but started 17th because of his engine penalty and charged all the way through to the podium, gaining 14 places and joining McLaren team-mate Norris in passing Antonelli right at the end. Kimi Antonelli - 9.5/10 Fastest of everyone in qualifying and a genuine contender for victory despite starting sixth because of his engine penalty. Battled Verstappen superbly before his Mercedes' energy deployment problem on the final lap cost him two places, although he still recovered fourth from Pierre Gasly before the flag. Pierre Gasly - 9/10 An excellent weekend and comfortably Alpine's best result of the season. Reached Q3, stayed with the leading group throughout and was less than three seconds away from victory at the finish. Franco Colapinto - 8.5/10 Another huge result for Alpine. Qualified inside the top 10, stayed out of trouble while plenty around him didn't and converted ninth on the grid into sixth place. Lewis Hamilton - 6.5/10 A messy weekend but there was still plenty of fight in the race. Missing Q3 was disappointing and the 10-second time penalty for passing Norris off the circuit was harsh, although being spun by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc later on was not his fault and he recovered to finish seventh. Carlos Sainz - 8.5/10 A superb recovery from 20th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. Kept himself in contention throughout, made up 12 places and even pinched eighth from Russell at the line to secure Williams' joint-best result of the season. item.title: Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'
item.description: The Ferrari drivers have previously compromised their own races while battling in Italy and Mexico this season [Getty Images] Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go, costing both points in a race where at one stage they were racing with the McLarens, which finished on the podium. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, which meant he finished 10th, three places behind Hamilton, in a race won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen. It was the second race-compromising incident within grands prix, and it came after the drivers had been brought together to clear the air at the last race in Brazil after their first-lap fighting in Mexico cost them a win. Hamilton said such an incident "should never happen" but added that: "The question should be for Ferrari now." Leclerc said: "We just need to fix whatever is not working." Team principal Frederic Vasseur described the situation as "completely unacceptable". Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide The Frenchman said: "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, the same speech as after Mexico. "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you're passed by others. It means you have to do your race and Charles clearly made a mistake. "It's penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable. Honestly we are more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico, we had a chat together in Brazil, today we passed the message to think about the team when racing together and the outcome is this one." The battle between the two drivers has been tense all season, and in the second part of the year there have been a series of flashpoints, whether it be on-track racing, disputes about how best to work through strategy, and Hamilton ignoring two separate calls to pit in different races, both of which compromised his result, because he was looking at beating Leclerc. Hamilton said: "It's not something I want to really get into." The seven-time champion, who struggled against Leclerc last year but who has been revived in 2026, deflected questions about whether he should be given number-one status. "I've never asked to be number one," he said. "I genuinely haven't ever asked. "There was a point in the season where I was 40-odd points ahead, and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi (Antonelli). "I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year. "At that point, we needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few instances in the season where, with the support, I think we could have beaten Kimi. "But no, that's not what I've asked for. We shouldn't have gotten together. That should just never happen. But I've said everything I can on it, and the question should

item.title: Serie A: Atalanta vs. Inter – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV
item.description: Serie A: Atalanta vs. Inter – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV Lautaro Martinez returns from injury, but is expected to start on the bench as Inter visit Maurizio Sarri’s Atalanta. It kicks off at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT] at the Gewiss Stadium in Bergamo. The defending Serie A champions must cope without Ange-Yoan Bonny and Piotr Zielinski, but Lautaro will be available for the first time in over a month. MILAN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 08: Marcus Thuram of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammate Francesco Pio Esposito during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Como 1907 at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 08, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Argentine returned to group training earlier this week, but may still start on the bench as the Nerazzurri face a tight fixture list ahead. Sky Sport and Gazzetta claim that Marcus Thuram and Francesco Pio Esposito will lead Inter’s attack in Bergamo tonight. Zielinski will be replaced by either Petar Sucic or Curtis Jones, while Benjamin Pavard is expected to start in a three-man defence, letting Manuel Akanji rest. BERGAMO, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Jonathan Rowe of Atalanta BC competes for the ball with Ze’ Pedro of Cagliari Calcioduring the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Parma Calcio at Stadio Atleti Azzurri d’Italia on September 12, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Home side Atalanta lack depth at the back, missing Odilon Kossounou and Isak Hien, while Jonathan Rowe is expected to start on the left wing, facing off against his English compatriot Djed Spence. Atalanta vs. Inter – where to watch on TV The match is available on TNT Sports 1, DAZN and HBO Max in the UK and Ireland and on Paramount+ in the USA. Football Italia will provide updates via a live blog. This match will kick off right after Milan-Frosinone. Atalanta vs. Inter – probable line-ups Inter (3-5-2): Martinez; Pavard, Bisseck, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Jones, Dimarco; M. Thuram, P. Esposito. item.title: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe
item.description: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe “Juni Calafat and Jose Angel Sanchez gave me a list of 4-5 strikers to choose from in the summer. I chose Carlos Espi.” These were the words of Jose Mourinho after Real Madrid’s win over Celta Vigo last night, a game in which Carlos Espi came off the bench to score the winner, and not for the first time. The manager heavily praised the new signing for his impact, and understandably so given how he has always found a way to come up clutch for Real Madrid, with his numbers being phenomenal. The best in the world As reported by AS , Espi is the most potent goalscoring substitute in all of Europe, and his efficiency in front of goal is second to none, especially under pressure. Espi’s goals have all led to direct points. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) In just about 73 minutes of football for Real Madrid, he has already scored four goals, all of which came in clutch moments. He averages one goal every 18 minutes. What makes the statistics all the more appalling is that he has scored his four goals from just six shots on target and nine overall shots. His goals have directly helped Real Madrid secure six points in La Liga and two in the UEFA Champions League. Thriving under pressure Espi arrived at Real Madrid knowing full well that Kylian Mbappe would be ahead of him on the pecking order. His role was always going to be one of a substitute, and he has embraced that role with minimal fuss. Espi is thriving under pressure. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Yet, the youngster is seemingly enjoying the responsibility of going out and making a difference in chaotic moments, especially with the clock ticking down. Having the manager’s trust as a player who can make a difference under pressure, after all, is something that can make a player supremely confident. Despite not having regular starts, Espi is thus impressing and making the most of his limited minutes at a range that not many saw coming. It remains to be seen if the manager finds any occasional starting role for Espi, especially given how he blatantly refused the possibility of fielding Mbappe and Espi together. What is for sure, however, is that Real Madrid have a pearl on their hands – one that they would likely not trade for any sum of money.

item.title: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top
item.description: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top The win in the Lower Rhine region was no footballing masterclass, but it was further proof of the resilience of Niko Kovac’s team. Gladbach put BVB under pressure with aggressive pressing, particularly in the first half. The Black & Yellows made technical errors, misplaced passes and found few ways to stretch the opposition defence. Although Felix Nmecha had a chance to put them ahead after just five minutes, BVB generally lacked pace and precision. “We weren’t sharp enough in the first half,” admitted the eventual goalscorer. Sporting director Ole Book also noted unnecessary losses of possession that could not be attributed solely to the hosts’ aggressive approach. With patience and, once again, the right substitutions The picture changed after the break. Borussia Dortmund increased the tempo, took more risks and pushed Gladbach increasingly deep into their own half. Once again, Niko Kovac showed a deft touch with his substitutions. Joey Veerman, Mathis Albert and Marcel Sabitzer were all involved in the build-up to the decisive goal. Albert played in Sabitzer, who laid the ball off for Nmecha. The Germany international unleashed a powerful shot from 19 metres to make it 1-0. It was Nmecha’s fifth goal of the season, already a personal best. The timing is also notable: the midfielder has scored three of his five goals in the final 15 minutes. BVB clearly have the patience and the physical reserves to make a decisive impact even in the closing stages. “We’ve scored late goals a lot now because we have the energy to keep playing our game right to the end,” explained goalkeeper Gregor Kobel. In fact, eight of the Black & Yellows’ 17 Bundesliga goals so far have come in the final ten minutes of matches. Almost half their goals have therefore come at a point when other teams are often already running out of energy and concentration. The fact that BVB left it late in Gladbach did not, however, mean the victory was undeserved. After a laboured first half, the Black & Yellows created considerably more chances. They finished with 2.5 expected goals to Gladbach’s 0.7. “Not spectacular, but deserved — in the manner of a top team,” was Book’s apt assessment. Only one defence in the league has conceded fewer than ten Nine narrow wins in total, including seven consecutive victories by exactly one goal: this has long since become more than a passing coincidence. Their last more comfortable victory was the 3-0 win over Paderborn. Since then, Borussia Dortmund have come out on top in seven of eleven tight encounters — in both the Bundesliga and the UEFA Champions League — alongside three draws and one defeat. Asked whether winning tight games had now become a particular Dortmund strength, Book replied: “If it is, we’ll certainly take it.” Of course, the team would prefer to put games to bed earlier. item.title: Victor Wembanyama admits his 50-point game was to ‘show off’ for Selena Gomez
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama subtly dedicated one moment from his 50-point explosion to Selena Gomez. The struggling New Orleans Pelicans had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs during their recent matchup. After all, Wembanyama exploded for 50 points and 18 rebounds in the 114-91 win in the Western Conference clash. Wemby’s 50-point game happened in the presence of longtime Spurs supporter and pop star Selena Gomez. Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama admits he wanted to show off in front of Selena Gomez After the game, Wembanyama was asked about one specific moment from the game, when he nailed a corner three-point shot and looked back at the crowd. As expected, Wembanyama did that for none other than Gomez, as the Spurs superstar made the admission during the postgame press conference. “Of course I had to show off for Selena, you know,” Wembanyama said while smiling. Despite being one of the biggest names in the NBA right now, he couldn’t avoid showing off in front of a star of Gomez’s caliber. Either way, Spurs fans will be happy as the team has now improved to a 14-3 record and remains tied with the Los Angeles Lakers in the Western Conference standings. item.title: Espi: “I will make the most of every minute to help the team”
item.description: Real Madrid hero Carlos Espí talked to the media after scoring yet another game-winning goal for the team, his third of this 2026-27 La Liga season. “I get goosebumps. It’s indescribable how much support I feel from everyone. I will give my all for the madridistas and for this club. I try to do what the coach asks of me, and every minute I get, I will make the most of it. If I can help the team, even better,” he said. Espí is fully aware of his role as an option off the bench, so his mindset and focus when his name is called is there at all times. “As I said the other day, the goal is to stay united. We’re 23-24 players, and we all need to move in the same direction. Those of us who came on did so fully focused on securing the victory, and that’s what we achieved,” he explained.

item.title: Roberto De Zerbi hails 'special' Luca Williams-Barnett and compares Tottenham wonderkid to Barcelona's Lamine Yamal following Ipswich masterclass
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has heaped praise on teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett following his match-winning full debut. The 18-year-old inspired Spurs to a 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday, scoring the opener before providing a sublime assist for Dominic Solanke. Academy graduate seizes his Premier League chance Calls for the England Under-19 international to feature had grown louder during a testing 12 months at Spurs, over a year after his senior bow at 16. Following two bright substitute cameos, De Zerbi finalised plans 10 days before Saturday's clash against Ipswich to hand him a maiden top-flight start. Williams-Barnett struck the opener on 15 minutes before embarking on a mazy second-half run to set up Solanke. De Zerbi outlines Maddison plan and defensive demands De Zerbi explained that pairing the teenager closely with James Maddison was key to his freedom, alongside strict instructions issued on Thursday regarding his defensive work rate. "Luca is a special player," De Zerbi said. "I'm not surprised, because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. I think he's lucky, because he's playing in a top club, with top teammates. "I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important. The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. "And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom. "And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers. Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch." YouTube inspiration fuels Yamal comparisons De Zerbi backed the 18-year-old to eventually match Barcelona prodigy Yamal, pointing to his relaxed preparation on the team bus as evidence of his rare mentality. "Yes, I think so," when asked whether Williams-Barnett can reach Yamal's level. "And one of the best things in my career... I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, [Eden] Hazard, Neymar. "I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?" Balancing flair with graft as expectations rise After turning brief cameos into a decisive full debut, Williams-Barnett now faces the task of cementing a regular starting berth alongside experienced teammates like Maddison and Solanke. item.title: Lewis Hamilton reacts to another clash with Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc: ‘I’ve done all I can’
item.description: Lewis Hamilton insists Ferrari needs to “sort out” how their drivers go racing after the Briton and Charles Leclerc collided once again at the Las Vegas Grand Prix . Three weeks on from their high-profile incident in Mexico City , which prompted a furious reaction from Hamilton, the Ferrari drivers clashed again on Saturday night in Sin City as they tussled for a handful of points. While fighting in the bottom half of the top-10, Leclerc surged down the inside at turn seven and Hamilton clipped his wheel, spinning the British driver. Hamilton in the end finished seventh, while Leclerc finished 10th after receiving a 10-second penalty from the stewards for the incident. Hamilton, who has implored his Ferrari outfit to clarify their policy when it comes to team orders, was level-headed after the race but acknowledged that the Scuderia need to clarify racing rules between the two drivers. “I’m not going to get into the scenario - that’s something to speak to Ferrari about,” he told Sky Sports F1 after the race, which was won by Red Bull ’s Max Verstappen . “We knew we were faced with another challenge today. The race I felt great, progressing well, I wanted to finish ahead of the McLarens; that’s who we’re fighting in constructors.” Hamilton himself had earlier been given a 10-second penalty for “leaving the track and gaining an unfair advantage” as he cut the corner in battle with both McLaren drivers, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. ”Avoiding a collision with the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty, which was really harsh,” he said. “Again got knocked back, never gave up, trying to get the best results. I think we could’ve got a podium.” Asked specifically about the racing rules with Leclerc, Hamilton replied: “That’s for Ferrari to decide. I’ve done all I can, I’ve said everything and more. It’s been difficult. “All I can do is show up and give everything I can, and hopefully in the background they can sort it all out.” Hamilton and Charles Leclerc clashed in Vegas (PA) Leclerc, meanwhile, was crestfallen in his post-race interview and admitted he felt “embarrassed” for the team after the collision. ”I’ve been penalised, so as a result, the majority thought it was my mistake,” he said. “I’ll accept that. I’m not going to say anymore. I was penalised; it has to be my mistake.” “I feel quite embarrassed for the team in general. We’ll review.” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur, meanwhile, declared the incident “completely unacceptable.” "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, the same speech as after Mexico,” he said. "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you're passed by others. It means you have to do your race and Charles clearly made a mistake. "It's penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable. item.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
item.description: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

item.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
item.description: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.

item.title: Expected Goals stats tell the very real story after Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2
item.description: Harvey Barnes Shooting Goal Newcastle v Arsenal Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game. To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing. Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match. With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value. The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot. The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match. So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc. These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48 As you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one. When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall. As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical. Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 – Saturday 21 November 2026 5.30pm Match Stats Goals: Newcastle United : Barnes 49, Thiaw 62 Arsenal : Eze 33 Madueke 78 Possession was Newcastle 34% Arsenal 66% Total shots were Newcastle 12 Arsenal 13 Shots on target were Newcastle 3 Arsenal 4 Corners were Newcastle 6 Arsenal 3 Touches in the opposition box Newcastle 15 Arsenal 24 Newcastle United team v Arsenal: Hornicek, Dedic (Livramento 46), Thiaw, Burn, Hall (Botman 92), Miley, Steur (Ramsey 46), Barnes, Willock (Wissa 83), Murphy (Elanga 46), Osula Unused subs: Pope, Schar, Gonzalez, Fernandez-Pardo

item.description: India A vs Pakistan Shaheens ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars score, toss winner, winning probability, result and highlights from Doha originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY MATCH DETAILS: (India A vs. Pakistan Shaheens) Venue: West End Park International Cricket Stadium, Doha Match: 8th Match, Group B, ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 (50 overs, day-night) Captains: Tilak Varma ( India A ), Abdul Samad ( Pakistan Shaheens ) Start time: 3:30 p.m. IST, with the toss at 3:00 p.m. IST Toss result: Pakistan won the toss (Bat first) Live Telecast: Sony Sports Network, SonyLIV (India) Umpires and match officials: TBD Match result: TBD Player of the Match: TBD India A vs. Pakistan Shaheens live match scorecard Follow the latest live scorecard here as the match unfolds, or click here for key text commentary updates . India A vs. Pakistan Shaheens Live Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the Group B match between India A and Pakistan Shaheens at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha. Toss result: Pakistan Shaheens won the toss and opted to bat first. Pre-match: India A and Pakistan Shaheens meet in Doha on Sunday with both sides unbeaten after one match apiece, which means the winner takes control of Group B with a game still to come against the loser of the morning fixture between the UAE and Nepal. India A arrived off the back of the largest winning margin in the history of List A cricket. Tilak Varma made 107 and Kumar Kushagra 117 as they posted 332 for 9 against Nepal on Friday, and Nepal were then bowled out for 26 in reply, with Prince Yadav taking 5 for 6 and Harshit Rana 4 for 16 in a 306-run win. Pakistan Shaheens opened with a 61-run win over the UAE on the same day, a more ordinary afternoon than India A's but one that leaves the two sides level on two points and separated only by net run rate. This is also the first meeting between the countries at any level since the Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, where the two captains walked out for the toss without a handshake. The BCCI's no-handshake protocol has held in every India-Pakistan fixture since the 2025 Asia Cup, including at this tournament last November. The tournament has moved to a 50-over format this year after being played as a T20 competition in its first edition, which is why India A have brought a squad built around batting depth rather than finishers. item.title: Noni Madueke: That wasn’t good enough
item.description: Noni Madueke: That wasn’t good enough Despite scoring the goal that rescued a point, Noni Madueke was left frustrated by the way Arsenal allowed control of the game to slip at Newcastle. Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Noni Madueke has admitted Arsenal ’s start to the second half against Newcastle United “wasn’t good enough” after the visitors had to come from behind to earn a 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite dominating the first half. Madueke scored Arsenal’s equaliser in the 78th minute, but his reaction afterwards told of the frustration within in the Arsenal camp after they let the game get away from them. Arsenal had been the significantly better side before the break and went ahead through Eberechi Eze in the 33rd minute. Madueke felt they had created enough opportunities to put themselves in a stronger position and included himself among those who should have done better. “I think we’re a little bit disappointed that we didn’t come away with three points, especially with how well we played in the first half,” Madueke said . Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images “We had opportunities to win the game, myself included, but that’s football. “I think the way we came out in the second half wasn’t good enough from our part, but we showed character to get a point in the end. “We take it, we move on, we watch the film back, and see where we can improve.” In what was a classic ‘game of two halves’, Harvey Barnes equalised four minutes into the second half before Malick Thiaw put Newcastle ahead in the 62nd minute after Arsenal had suffocated the Magpies in the first half. Madueke’s goal 16 minutes later prevented Arsenal leaving empty-handed, but he did not allow the equaliser to disguise the frustration at their second half performance. Speaking to BBC Match of the Day , he said , “A draw at St James’ Park is not the end of the world but it’s disappointing. “I think we let it slip. They came out with more intensity and fight but I feel it was on us. The principles and concepts we played with in the first half weren’t there at the start of the second.” Photo by George Wood/Getty Images His assessment to Sky Sports followed the same line. Madueke said Arsenal had been “outstanding” before half-time, only for their level to drop during the opening 20 minutes of the second half. He questioned whether they had become “too relaxed” after the quality of their first-half display, although he ultimately said 2-2 was a fair result. Madueke also had chances before the break which he felt he should have taken, so scoring the equaliser did not leave him entirely satisfied with his own evening. “I missed a couple of chances in the first half so that kind of brought me back to neutral,” he said. Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Arsenal had shown enough quality to take control of the game and enough character to recover once Newcastle had turned it around, but Madueke felt the drop in standards after the interval had cost them. item.title: ‘Dissed Luka (Dončić),’ ‘Calling Out (LeBron James)’ — NBA Fans Try to Crack Who Victor Wembanyama Targeted With ‘Stat-Padding’ Jab
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) looks over in the first half against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center. © Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama exploded for 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks, and 4 steals in 32 minutes as the San Antonio Spurs pulled away from the New Orleans Pelicans for a 114-91 win on Saturday night at Frost Bank Center. It was the franchise star’s remark about padding stats in his on-court interview afterward, though, that set off a guessing game amongst the fans. Victor Wembanyama’s Stat-Padding Remark Has Fans Pointing at Luka Dončić, LeBron James Wembanyama shot 20-of-29 from the field, including 5-of-11 from 3-point range, and became the third player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks in a game. It was his second 50-point night this season and the third of his career, tying David Robinson for second in Spurs history behind George Gervin’s five. Asked on the court after the final buzzer about reaching 50 points, Wembanyama said, “It is very special.” Then, with a smile, he added, “But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” He named no one in that answer, but it did not take long for fans to fill in the blanks. One fan was blunt, writing , “Wemby DISSED Luka after his 50-point game.” Dončić leads the league at 37.2 points per game and already has two 50-point games this season, the same number as Wembanyama. Another fan landed in the same place, writing , “Wemby just called Luka a stat-padder.” Another fan took the comment as a shot at LeBron James as well, posting , “Calling out Bron and Luka. Love this guy.” James had 21 points, six assists, and six rebounds in the Philadelphia 76ers’ 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks. NBA Memes skipped past the question of whom he meant and looked ahead to a bigger fight later in the season between the two stars. “Luka vs. Wemby for MVP could be an all-time battle,” the fan wrote. One observer expected plenty more where that came from, writing, “Whew, when this man start winning chip or after his first. Y’all will see some nasty words coming out his mouth. Will be name-calling everyone one by one.” Asked by reporters to elaborate on the remark later Saturday night, Wembanyama cited Dončić, James, Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić as examples of players who don’t worry about padding their stats. item.title: Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City must tighten up defensively after their winless run continued with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Fulham. City needed an equalizer from Elliot Anderson at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday to avoid a fourth successive Premier League defeat. Anderson’s volley just before the hour mark cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener and, although City were aggrieved that Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed, there was no disguising another disappointing display. City manager Maresca said: “For sure we are conceding too many goals. We need to avoid that. “Sometimes you need to win games 1-0, you need to keep clean sheets and unfortunately, at this moment, we are not able to do that. This is the main thing. “I think we concede almost 80%of our goals in the first 20 minutes, so for sure there is something there that we need to improve. “But I can see many positive aspects and this is something we started four months ago, not four years ago.” The main talking point of the game was referee Thomas Bramall’s decision to chalk off what would have been a leveller from Haaland in the 25th minute. The Norwegian bundled home from close range after Bernd Leno had failed to gather a shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. Haaland was perplexed, but the decision was upheld by VAR and the striker then uncharacteristically spurned another good chance soon after. It was left to Anderson to salvage a point for City from what was a largely lacklustre performance. The midfielder marked his return to action after being sent off for England last week when he struck with a low volley from the edge of the area after a corner was cleared. Anderson told the club’s website: “It was a poor first half, unfortunately. We seem to have been going behind recently, but the reaction was really good after half-time. “It just wasn’t enough to get the three points. We had plenty of chances, which seems to be the overall story [lately], but once they start going in, and as maybe we start picking our performances up a little bit more, we’ll be happy.” With Enzo Fernandez on the bench after returning later from international duty, Anderson was deployed in a more advanced role by Maresca. “I played a little bit higher up and got myself a goal,” Anderson said. “I’m just trying to just work on my game. “We tweaked a few things and really went for them, which gave us a bit more control of the game. It’s just unlucky we didn’t get the second.”

item.title: 'Help the team massively': CSK star hails team's decision to appoint MS Dhoni as mentor after retirement ahead of IPL 2027
item.description: 'Help the team massively': CSK star hails team's decision to appoint MS Dhoni as mentor after retirement ahead of IPL 2027 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Noor Ahmad says MS Dhoni's mentor role will help Chennai Super Kings in a big way. The Afghanistan spinner named Dhoni's stumpings and finishing as what the side will miss. Dhoni ended his IPL playing career at the retention deadline and will become CSK 's mentor from 2027. Noor Ahmad backs CSK's decision to keep MS Dhoni on as team mentor Chennai Super Kings announced two things on the IPL 2027 retention deadline day. One, that Mahendra Singh Dhoni formally retired as a player and that he would be the team's mentor from 2027. Noor Ahmad, who has spent the last two seasons bowling under him at Chepauk, was asked about the appointment while playing for Dubai Capitals in the DP World ILT20. His answer put the emphasis on continuity rather than farewell. "Everyone will miss him, but his new role is going to help the team massively, and I am happy that he is still with the team," the 21-year-old told PTI in Dubai, in comments reported by Siasat . Asked what he would miss most about having Dhoni in the side, he did not reach for the captaincy or the aura. "There are many things, but I would say his stumping, maybe, and his finishing abilities," Noor said. MORE: CSK auction targets: Who will they buy in IPL 2027 mini-auction? What Chennai Super Kings lose with MS Dhoni no longer behind the stumps In practice, they lost most of it a season ago. Dhoni did not play a single match in IPL 2026 as recurring injuries kept him out, and Chennai finished eighth with six wins from 14 matches without him. The transition had been running for longer than that. He handed the captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad before the 2024 season and spent the years after it as a batter who came in for the last few overs rather than a man who shaped a side from behind the stumps. What he leaves behind is a record no CSK player will approach. Five IPL titles as captain, two Champions League T20 titles on top of them, and a run with the franchise that began in 2008 and was interrupted only by the two seasons at Rising Pune Supergiant while Chennai served their suspension. MORE: IPL 2027: Cummins to play for SRH in upcoming season - Report Why Noor Ahmad will feel MS Dhoni's absence more than most at CSK The two things Noor named are not a coincidence. A left-arm wrist-spinner lives off batters coming down the pitch and not getting back, and the keeper standing up is the one who converts that into a wicket rather than a leg-bye. Chennai have covered the position well. Sanju Samson arrived in the trade that took Ravindra Jadeja and Sam Curran to Rajasthan Royals and is among the better Indian keepers standing up to spin, with Urvil Patel behind him, so Noor is not bowling to a novice in 2027. item.title: Max Verstappen labels George Russell a ‘joke’ and ‘so far below my level’ in stinging remarks
item.description: Max Verstappen declared that George Russell was “so far below my level” in a series of stinging remarks about his Formula 1 rival after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix . The duo, who clashed in a series of heated confrontations on track and in the media at the end of the 2024 season, have reignited their rivalry this weekend in Las Vegas after an incident in final practice on Saturday. Russell stated that Verstappen “screwed him over” after the pair collided, adding that the Dutchman believes he is “bigger and better than everyone else.” The pair started on the front row and astonishingly traded places with Russell 12 times during a breathless race in Sin City. Yet with a handful of laps remaining, Russell misjudged an overtake on teammate Kimi Antonelli and hit the barrier. Verstappen stormed to victory while the Briton finished down in ninth. "Ha ha, well done! My God," laughed Verstappen on team radio when the incident occurred. Then, in an interview with Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay, Verstappen took aim at Russell. "This actually had nothing to do with Formula 1," he said "But I did enjoy some of the action. Especially because one person in particular didn't stand a chance. He [Russell] deserves that too. “His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me. All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect Karma." Speaking later in the FIA press conference, Verstappen elaborated: "It doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. "So it doesn't bother me. And today, Karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. "I was like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Verstappen and Russell also clashed last year after the Dutchman deliberately rammed the Mercedes driver at the Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona. In a season where the majority had Russell as the pre-season favourite, his Mercedes teammate Antonelli has romped to the world championship while second-placed Verstappen is now 40 points clear of Russell with two rounds remaining. The next round is the Qatar Grand Prix on 29 November.

item.title: Bayern Munich legend rebukes club over the Jamal Musiala situation
item.description: FC Bayern have made headlines this past week as the club’s management has opened a wildly insensitive public dialogue about Jamal Musiala’s health and contract with the club. Many have rushed to critici ze this approach, and club legend Lothar Matthäus is the next to join the list. Speaking to Sky Sport after Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln, Matthäus delivered a scathing critique of the various statements made by those in charge at Bayern. “I’ve actually been a bit shocked throughout this entire week. It started with Uli Hoeneß, continued with Jan-Christian Dreesen, and yesterday Kar l-Heinz Rummenigge chose the strongest words of all. I have enormous respect for Karl-He inz. I’ve known him for over 30 years. He’s a wonderful person. But, of course, those were statements he chose v ery deliberately,” said Matthäus (as captured via @iMiaSanMia ). He continued: “We’ve been praising FC Bayern for the past two years, saying that it’s a big family with a strong sense of unity. That has also been evident, and it’s why these results have been possible. Why don’t [Jamal Musiala’s camp and FC Bayern] simply sit down together in private an d sort this out instead of doing it in public? We haven’t heard anything from Musiala’s ca mp. His camp hasn’t held any talks with FC Bayern yet. FC Bayern hasn’t approached Musiala’s camp either. I think it’s absolu tely essential that they do so now, before this continues over the coming days and weeks. Because the person who suf fers most from all this is Jamal Musiala! He’s the one under pressure, the one expected to deliver, especially with so many players injured at th e club.” His final remark was perhaps the most important one: “Talk to each other and find a solution!” Discussions between both partie s must ensue quickly to try and save a situation that has already gotten far out of hand. It isn’t often that Matthäus makes rational arguments, but he is absolutely right in this case. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Barcelona face fresh hurdle in pursuit of key target as his club demand more than €20m – report
item.description: Barcelona face fresh hurdle in pursuit of key target as his club demand more than €20m – report According to SPORT , Barcelona have stepped up their efforts to sign Ruud Nijstad from FC Twente ahead of the January transfer window, but the Dutch club are making an agreement difficult. The 18-year-old centre-back has become one of the Catalan giants’ preferred defensive targets , but any move for the youngster will be complicated due to Twente’s demands. Nijstad open to Barcelona move Having already tried to sign Nijstad in the summer, Barcelona have renewed contact with Twente in an attempt to revive the operation in the January transfer window. Nijstad was initially inclined to continue his development in the Netherlands, but his position has softened after learning more about the sporting project being offered by the La Liga champions. The 18-year-old starlet is particularly attracted by Barcelona’s willingness to give opportunities to emerging players. As such, he sees the Blaugrana as the ideal environment to continue his development, making a move to Camp Nou increasingly appealing. Barcelona want Nijstad in January. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) While this is an encouraging development as far as Barcelona are concerned, convincing the player is only part of the challenge. Twente demand more than €20 million Indeed, as per the report, Twente’s financial demands are making the transfer increasingly complicated. The Dutch club have raised their asking price and are now demanding more than €20 million to sanction his departure. A left-footed centre-back with an impressive ability to play out from the back, Barça see the teenager as a good fit into their tactical setup. However, Barcelona consider that figure excessive for an 18-year-old who still has relatively limited experience at the highest level. Although the Catalans are convinced by Nijstad’s potential, they are reluctant to commit such a substantial amount to a player whose development is far from complete. Barcelona do not want to spend big on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Moreover, Twente want to retain Nijstad until the end of the current campaign, even if they agree to sell him during the January window. The Dutch club would consider negotiating a permanent transfer in January on the condition that the teenage defender returns to them on loan until June. For Barcelona, however, the idea does not fit with their intention to bring Nijstad in during the winter window, making the possibility of a deal extremely difficult. Beyond these two complications, Barcelona also have to deal with the fact hat the youngster is attracting interest from the Premier League. Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United are all monitoring Nijstad’s development, and their interest could make an already difficult negotiation even more complex.

item.title: 'We're underdogs': New MI coach makes honest admission ahead of IPL 2027 season
item.description: 'We're underdogs': New MI coach makes honest admission ahead of IPL 2027 season originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Robin Uthappa has been appointed Mumbai Indians ' batting coach ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He says the five-time champions feel like underdogs and must earn back supporters' trust. Mumbai finished ninth in 2026 and have gone six seasons without a title. Robin Uthappa says Mumbai Indians feel like underdogs going into IPL 2027 Five titles usually buy a franchise some patience, but Mumbai Indians have not won one since 2020 and finished ninth last season with four wins from 14 matches. Their new batting coach is not pretending otherwise. Robin Uthappa, who took the job as part of a wholesale change to the coaching staff, framed the coming season in terms most people associate with a struggling side rather than the most decorated in the competition. "As Mumbai Indians, we feel like we're underdogs," he said in an interaction with select media, reported by NDTV . He went further on what the squad owes the people who follow it. "We really need to earn our stripes back and earn the trust of the fans. There are a lot of things that we have to work towards as a team," Uthappa added. The appointment itself caught him off guard. "It completely came from left field. I didn't see it coming," said the two-time IPL winner, who is currently commentating at the DP World ILT20 in the UAE, adding that he had been hoping for a call from the franchise because he believed he could add value to it. MORE: MI likely auction targets: Who will they buy in IPL 2027 mini-auction? What Mumbai Indians have changed after six seasons without an IPL title Uthappa is one piece of an overhaul that has touched almost every part of the setup. Kieron Pollard, who held the batting role last season, has been elevated to head coach, former India fielding coach T Dilip takes the fielding brief, and Mitchell McClenaghan returns to the franchise as bowling coach. The playing side has moved just as far. Hardik Pandya, who captained through the ninth-place finish, has gone to Punjab Kings in the trade that brought Arshdeep Singh the other way, and Mumbai have changed captain for 2027, with Rohit Sharma widely reported to be taking the job back. Uthappa's answer to all of it was to talk about humility rather than personnel. "Nobody is bigger than Mother Cricket. We've all been in the game long enough to know that nobody can beat Mother Cricket. You have to operate from that humility," he said. He described his own role as a supporting one rather than a corrective one. "I'm only a mirror to them, holding them accountable for what they want to achieve and aligning that with the larger goal of the team," Uthappa said. item.title: Hawks Hits: Rinzel Makes History, Fighting Through Adversity, Frondell Injured
item.description: Nearly two full months into the season, the Chicago Blackhawks finally earned their first road win in 10 tries on Saturday night, defeating the Calgary Flames 4-3 in overtime at Scotiabank Saddledome. The Blackhawks were the only NHL team still without a road win entering Saturday, and they had to overcome plenty of adversity to change that in Calgary. The countless hardships and seemingly never-ending misfortune in the first quarter of this season are starting to harden the young Hawks group. Already without captain Connor Bedard in the lineup for the second straight game due to his latest shoulder injury , the Blackhawks also lost defenseman Wyatt Kaiser and center Anton Frondell on Saturday, leaving only 16 skaters for the third period and overtime. With a shortened visiting bench, and the Flames carrying all the momentum late after clawing back from a 3-1 deficit, the Blackhawks dug deep to push the game to 3-on-3 play. Then, after Frank Nazar drew a penalty with a tremendous solo effort, the power play converted just after Yegor Sharangovich stepped out of the penalty box, with Sam Rinzel fittingly responsible for the game-winner. “I thought our guys, with the loss of Frondell and Kaiser, we had to gut it out. Especially after giving up the early goal in the third [period]. It wasn’t necessarily our best third, but we found a way to bend not break.” Another obstacle the Hawks faced was an overturned overtime-winner from Roman Kantserov , who became the first NHL rookie to reach 10 goals this season earlier in the game. Kantserov’s net-front tap-in from Patrick Kane ‘s pass was reversed for a careless offside by Nazar, setting the stage for another potential disastrous loss that would have perfectly described the tumultuous season thus far. But despite all the bumps in the road, the Blackhawks stuck with it and found a second game-winning goal in overtime, with no dispute from the Flames or video review necessary for Rinzel’s tally. Since the disastrous three-game Southeastern road trip and GM Kyle Davidson’s state-of-the-union press conference, the Blackhawks have done well to smooth the waters around a rocking ship. They’re now 3-1-1 in the last five games, and all three wins have been character-builders. Their win over the Buffalo Sabres on Nov. 12 marked the first time they earned two points when trailing entering the third period this season. That victory was particularly needed, considering it was the Hawks’ first game after an embarrassing 9-2 loss in Carolina. Then, when Bedard got injured in Tuesday’s game against the Toronto Maple Leafs, the Blackhawks didn’t let it take the wind out of their sails and sealed the win for their captain, scoring a season-high six goals. Now, the Blackhawks have won away from the United Center for the first time this year, which should give the group added confidence that they can do it again on Sunday in Vancouver. The back end of the back-to-back comes against the 32nd-ranked Canucks, presenting anot

item.title: 'Right now Malen is extraordinary!' - Gian Piero Gasperini explains how former Aston Villa striker matched a 66-year Roma record with four-goal Parma demolition
item.description: FBL-ITA-SERIE A-PARMA-ROMA - AFP Donyell Malen netted four goals in Roma's 5-1 Serie A demolition of Parma to equal an all-time club record for calendar-year league strikes. Coach Gian Piero Gasperini hailed the former Aston Villa forward as "extraordinary" after his 26th Serie A goal of 2026 kept the Giallorossi within two points of leaders Lazio. Malen hits four to equal 66-year Roma record Donyell Malen scored four times to inspire Roma to an emphatic 5-1 Serie A victory over Parma and keep Gian Piero Gasperini's side just two points behind league leaders Lazio. Rodrigo Mora added Roma's other goal after Nesta Elphege had briefly equalised on the counter-attack for the hosts. The four-goal haul took Malen to 12 goals in the opening 12 league rounds and 26 Serie A strikes across the 2026 calendar year since arriving from Aston Villa in January. That tally draws the Netherlands international level with Pedro Manfredini's all-time club record set in 1960, with more than a month of the year still remaining. Gasperini explains why Malen thrives in his system Speaking to DAZN Italia after the final whistle, Gasperini praised his team's response to conceding an equaliser and singled out Malen's tactical compatibility with Roma's attacking style. "Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, you don't play at that level without quality," Gasperini said. "Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way. There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents, and of course Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary. He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn't fit as well with our style of football." From Villa loanee to record-breaking talisman Malen initially joined Roma on loan from Aston Villa on 16 January 2026 before completing a permanent €25 million move in May on a contract running until June 2030 after firing the club back into the UEFA Champions League. His latest four-goal outing also marked his third Serie A hat-trick of 2026—a feat last achieved in the Italian top flight by Josip Ilicic, who also played under Gasperini at Atalanta. Roma's 36 goals across their first 12 league fixtures represent the highest total by any Serie A team in 76 years, since Inter, Milan and Juventus all surpassed that mark in the 1950-51 season. Title race momentum builds with fixtures left in 2026 With Roma sitting on 30 points and chasing Lazio at the summit, Gasperini noted that overcoming adversity at Parma showed his squad's growing belief. For Malen, standing level with Manfredini on 26 calendar-year league goals in late November leaves ample opportunity to claim the all-time Roma record outright before 2026 concludes.

item.title: Stark reality of Sporting Director transfer dealings laid bare in front of Yasir Al-Rumayyan
item.description: Yasir Al-Rumayyan It was well-publicised ahead of the match that Yasir Al-Rumayyan would be at St James’ Park for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal. An up and down season so far for United. A chance for the Newcastle United Chairman to see for himself at close quarters how things are now looking. Yasir Al-Rumayyan seeing a game of two halves. Newcastle United struggling to get out of their own half in the opening 45 minutes as Arsenal dominated and led 1-0 at the break. Matthias Jaissle making three substitutions at the break and a totally different Newcastle United on show, by far the better team that ‘won’ the second half 2-1. By the final whistle, Newcastle United had certainaly deserved at least a point, possibly all three. The brilliant second half comeback was achieved due to the following 13 Newcastle United players and these 13 can be separated as follows: Already at St James’ Park pre-Eddie Howe: Lewis Miley, Joe Willock Signed by Eddie Howe: Tino Livramento, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Yoane Wissa, Anthony Elanga, William Osula Ross Wilson signings: Lukas Hornicek Ahead of summer 2026, Newcastle United Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan took control of transfers from Eddie Howe and gave it to Ross Wilson. Eddie Howe (and then Matthias Jaissle) still having some say but Ross Wilson the one dictating the overall transfer policy and holding the power. This isn’t unusual, many clubs having a similar strategy of handing the Sporting Director control of transfer policy. Ross Wilson the key man this summer in deciding to sell Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, as well as not renewing the contracts of Kieran Trippier and a number of other older players. Altogether, approximately £260m/£270m was committed on new signings by Ross Wilson to rebuild the Newcastle United team and squad. Yasir Al-Rumayyan must have been wondering where they all were in that second half against Arsenal… Amar Dedic – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Sean Steur – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Nico Gonzalez – An unused sub Matias Fernandez-Pardo – An unused sub Bazoumana Toure – Left out of the matchday squad Aladji Bamba – Left out of the matchday squad Ewen Jaouen – Injured Ousmane Diabate – On loan for the season at Turkish top tier club Gençlerbirliği It is still early days and we need a lot longer to judge properly when it comes to allowing Ross Wilson control of transfers in and out. However, there are inherent weaknesses with a system whereby the Sporting Director and not the Manager/Head Coach has control of selecting which players are signed and which are sold/let go. As things stand, Matthias Jaissle clearly overwhelmingly feels he has to rely at this moment in time on players who came in before Ross Wilson’s summer of 2026. item.title: Indiana men's soccer's fitting into championship form: 'They came here for that'
item.description: BLOOMINGTON — Todd Yeagley isn’t shy about breaking one of coaching’s oldest and most trusted codes when he thinks the time is right. The head coach of his alma mater for close to two decades now, Yeagley will lead Indiana men’s soccer into yet another NCAA Tournament this weekend among the favorites to win the competition. Among the most decorated programs in the history of the sport, Indiana secured its 13 th Big Ten double — a regular-season and tournament title — with a dramatic win on penalties at home against Washington on Nov. 15, and the Hoosiers won’t leave Bloomington again unless or until they reach the College Cup . That victory over the Huskies helped cement Yeagley’s team as one of the tournament’s top four seeds, meaning IU will host every game it plays in the competition until the semifinal, which will be held in Cary, North Carolina next month. This is a familiar path for Indiana , whose 22 all-time appearances in the College Cup are a record. And that sky-high annual expectation is why Yeagley, breaking from the tried-and-tested coaching tradition of never talking big picture, is willing to acknowledge with his team all that it can achieve. “(Players) know what the goals of this program are,” Yeagley told IndyStar. “We win in big moments, and we want to be in position to fight for titles, and one has to come before the other. “We don’t talk about a Final Four, a national championship. They know that’s the goal. They came here for that.” It’s what they’ll start chasing at noon Sunday, when Indiana hosts Missouri State, which defeated Saint Louis 1-0 in the tournament’s first round Thursday night in Springfield, Missouri. The Hoosiers will have to navigate a draw that includes several familiar faces, including No. 2 seed Maryland, No. 3 seed Louisville and the same Washington team (now a 5 seed) Indiana dispatched in the Big Ten final. And they’ll lean on an experienced, veteran team to do it. One comprised of a healthy blend of homegrown players and transfers. And one build to attack opponents in a variety of ways. “(Indiana has) confident attackers, and it’s not, we need only one to be good every game. We’ve got several,” Yeagley said. “We’re not one-player dependent.” Yeagley’s versatile, dangerous front line reflects that roster blend that’s served the Hoosiers so well this fall. Collins Oduro, Easton Bogard and Charlie Heuer — homegrown players familiar to IU fans for several years now — combined for 18 goals and 10 assists, while transfers Oliver Moller-Jensen (Florida Atlantic) and Stephane Njike (Maryland) chipped in 15 and 11, respectively. Moller-Jensen leads all Hoosiers this season, with 13 goals in 20 games. Together, they fashion an attack that finished second in the Big Ten, with 41 goals. item.title: Five Oklahoma State football takeaways as Caleb Hawkins powers OT rally at Arizona State
item.description: TEMPE, AZ — Time in the injury tent and halftime locker room just made Caleb Hawkins stronger. Fighting an ankle injury that he tweaked in the first half at Arizona State , the Oklahoma State football star running back returned after halftime and led the Cowboys to a 30-27 overtime win over the Sun Devils on Saturday night. In the first half, the Cowboys ran 14 times for an average of 1.3 yards. Hawkins’ longest rush of the first half was 8 yards. The Doak Walker Award semifinalist who averages 117 yards per game went into halftime with seven carries for 19 yards. After halftime, he rushed 15 times for 85 yards (5.6 yards per carry). Despite trailing by 17 points at halftime, the Cowboys (7-4, 5-3 Big 12) didn't abandon the run. They embraced it. “He’s an alpha, for sure in every sense of the imagination," OSU coach Eric Morris said. "He loves football and loves to play the running back position. Plays it the right way, tough to tackle and so coming out of halftime, we wanted to be able to get him going downhill and let him go and do his thing.” Here are four more takeaways from the Cowboys' win: RECAP: Oklahoma State football survives Arizona State as Drew Mestemaker, Cowboys cap rally in OT A Big 12 After Dark game got strange Arizona State linebacker Martell Hughes ripped the ball away from Cowboy receiver Terrance Lewis for a turnover that was part interception and part fumble recovery. The turnover was something between an interception as Lewis high-pointed the football and Hughes (who outweighs Lewis by 60 pounds) got his arms on the ball as Lewis brought it into his body. By the time Lewis’ backside hit the grass, the ball was out of his possession. It went down as the third interception of Hughes’ career. In a Big 12 After Dark game that ended past 1 a.m. in Oklahoma, that was the first sign things were getting weird. The play was significant, too. It would have been a Cowboy first down in the red zone. Instead, the Sun Devils (6-5, 4-4) took the ball and scored on a 60 yard-touchdown pass. The deep pass was deflected off the hand of corner LaDainian Fields, who leads the country with seven interceptions this season, into the hands of receiver Reed Harris. In the third quarter, a review lasted several minutes to determine whether OSU corner Christian Bodnar recovered a fumble that bounced along the sideline. No replay angle down the sideline offered a definitive angle and Arizona State retained possession. Morris said referees gave an explanation for the call. What he left unsaid was the explanation left him unsatisfied. "I'm not even to go there, but we're going to have a lengthy discussion. the answers that were told to me, like... " The halftime deficit problem reaches a new low OSU has now trailed or been tied at the half in all but one big 12 game. item.title: Boise State CFP Picture Changes With Loss; Liberty, New Mexico, UTSA Notice
item.description: FORT COLLINS, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 7: Head coach Spencer Danielson of the Boise State Broncos celebrates after a touchdown in the first quarter of the game against the Colorado State Rams at Canvas Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Fort Collins, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) Getty Most college football fans were asleep when the game-winning field goal went through. But at about 1:10 a.m. ET, San Diego State drilled a 3-pointer at the buzzer to stun Boise State, 22-20. With that make came a potentially drastic shakeup to the College Football Playoff picture for Group of 6 teams. One Group of 6 team gets into this year’s 12-team field automatically, and it was shaping up to be the Broncos. All of a sudden, that’s not so certain. Fans of Liberty, New Mexico and UTSA are all watching closely. Boise State CFP Picture The reality is that Boise State, even with the loss, may remain in the driver’s seat for that spot, but with a lot less margin for error. The Broncos were ranked No. 17 this week by the CFP committee, and no other Group of 6 team was ranked in the top-25 at all. That would suggest the committee viewed the gap as pretty wide. Before this, Boise State’s only loss was to Oregon. Boise State will be watching closely to see where it slots this week. The Broncos have just one game left, the Pac-12 title game. If Boise State had won out, there would’ve been no question here. But with the surprise loss, the door has been opened up to the rest of the Group of 6. Group of 6 Playoff Picture: Liberty, New Mexico, UTSA If New Mexico hadn’t recently been upset by UNLV, the Lobos might have a chance to leapfrog Boise State right now. As is, these teams will all get a bit closer together. Liberty looks the best in a quick look on paper. They’re 10-1 with a 7-0 conference record and still a conference title game to play, but the Flames have also played a brutally poor schedule. That won’t do them any favors. New Mexico is still in the picture after a key win over Wyoming on Friday night. The American Conference leader, UTSA (Texas-San Antonio), is now 9-2 after Saturday and still alive here, too. These other Group of 6 teams would likely have their best chance if Boise State loses in their conference championship game in a couple of weeks. All these other contenders can do is close with wins and then hope. We’ll get a great hint on Tuesday night, though, when the CFP committee releases another rankings. Will Boise State still be in the top-25? Will a different Group of 6 team be there? There’s a lot still to be decided, and San Diego State’s stunning upset certainly left this door quite a bit more open. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Boise State CFP Picture Changes With Loss; Liberty, New Mexico, UTSA Notice appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Red Bull boss shrugs off war of words between Verstappen and Russell
item.description: Laurent Mekies cares little about the recent war of words between Max Verstappen and George Russell . After their FP3 incident, the British driver said that he will not accept the way Verstappen behaves on the race track. "Somebody's got to stand up to that guy! (...) I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this, and walk around like they are bigger and better than everybody else." After qualifying, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff also commented on the rivalry between the two drivers, saying that they might crash into each other after the start, as both drivers lined up on the front row of the grid. Moreover, Verstappen hit back after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver said : "It's not like a success today. The thing is he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures "And today, karma is a b****. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what's happening. So I was like, fantastic. My day is only getting better. And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Mekies doesn't care about all the noise After the race, the Red Bull boss was also asked about the matter. Speaking to GPblog , among others, he said: "I didn't hear neither what Max said nor what Toto said apparently. So I didn't hear, so I'm not sure what it is. "But is it a distraction? Because somebody already asked me on the grid today based on whatever was said yesterday. Distraction, zero. Honestly, our approach is we concentrate on racing. We take some pride to say that we don't care about the noise around, and that's that's how we consider it, the noise around, but... So zero distraction for us," he concluded.

item.title: Wembanyama hits 50 points in dominant Spurs win
item.description: Victor Wembanyama was selected by the San Antonio Spurs with the first overall pick in the 2023 NBA draft. [Reuters] San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama hit 50 points in a historic performance as his side beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91. The 22-year-old, who is 7ft 4ins tall, became the first player with 50 points, five blocks and five three-pointers in a match since the NBA added threes in 1979–80. The France international, who was defensive player of the year for 2026, said he put on a show for a celebrity-packed crowd which included actress and long-time Spurs fan Selena Gomez. "I had to show off for Selena," he said. "I just want to keep stacking them [records] up. I don't plan on doing those. They just come and we play the right way as a team. "So, I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there's many more coming." The Spurs have made a fine start to the season, winning 14 of their 17 games so far to top the Western Conference Southwest. They won the division last season before losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson added. "It's a cliche to say, 'Why doesn't he do it every game?' "But it's so interesting when people play like that, especially with his talent." 'I'm not very good at stat-padding' Wembanyama's haul - the third of his career - came after James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games on Saturday. Wilt Chamberlain holds the record with an incredible 118 50-point games. "It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat-padding," Wembanyama said. "So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have." Wembanyama was later asked whether there was an ethical right or wrong way to score 50 points. Some NBA players have been accused of chasing individual statistics for financial gain instead of concentrating on their team's results. "Maybe, I think that's a question for you. The greats, they don't think about that," Wembanyama replied. "I don't think LeBron [James], Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander], [Nikola] Jokic, [Luka] Doncic, I don't think they think about that. I have them as examples, so I'm trying to not think about it either."

item.title: ‘Troy (Aikman) Screwed Himself,’ ‘People Don’t Like Him’ — Ex-NFL Scout Makes Feelings Clear on Cowboys Legend’s Beef With Joe Buck Amid ESPN MNF Drama
item.description: Oct 26, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Troy Aikman looks on before the game between Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. © Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The reported tension between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck has continued to make noise despite ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro recently addressing the situation and praising both broadcasters. His latest comments surrounding the Monday Night Football duo have done little to quiet the discussion. Former NFL scout John Middlekauff has now questioned why Aikman has received little public support from his ESPN colleagues, even suggesting the Dallas Cowboys legend may have contributed to the problem himself. John Middlekauff Questions Why ESPN Crew Has Not Supported Troy Aikman Middlekauff addressed the situation on his podcast, “3 & OUT with John Middlekauff,” and questioned the source of some of those reports, suggesting that ESPN’s own broadcasting group was behind the negative coverage. “Jimmy Pitaro, who is the boss of ESPN, he said he was disappointed about the discourse around Troy Aikman in the media reports. It’s like, Jimmy, I read the article on The Athletic. All the stuff being leaked was clearly coming from your crew,” Middlekauff said . He suggested that if the former Cowboys quarterback was well-liked within the broadcasting group, at least some colleagues would have spoken publicly in his defense. “If you’re ever in a situation like this, where they’re choosing between two people, you would think there would be someone, if not multiple people, who, if they were on equal footing and well-liked, would come out and say, ‘Hey, I think it’s going to be a big loss. Troy’s a stud. We love Troy. We love working with Troy.’ There hasn’t been a peep. Not a single word of support for Troy Aikman.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor He also explained why he believes Aikman has directed much of his frustration toward Buck, despite the latter not being the person responsible for ESPN’s contract decisions. “He’s taking it all out on Joe, which I do understand from his standpoint. It’s like, ‘You left me in a life raft by myself. You screwed me,’” the former scout said. “But couldn’t you make the argument that Troy screwed himself? I just think Joe is the easy one for Troy to blame. He’s not the decision maker. Why haven’t these guys supported you?” Middlekauff concluded.
