item.title: Alabama’s Jett Thomalla Makes Statement on Future
item.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 17: Jett Thomalla #15 of the Alabama Crimson Tide warms up before his game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Camden Hall/Getty Images) Getty Most of Alabama’s game against Chattanooga on Saturday was just a matter of punching in at the time clock and taking care of business before the Iron Bowl next week. Jett Thomalla, though, had a different task. A legendary high school quarterback from Nebraska, Thomalla had flipped late in his recruiting cycle to the Crimson Tide, but he hadn’t yet played for Alabama in a regular season game. This was Thomalla’s chance. Keelon Russell sat out the game. Austin Mack played most of the way. But late in the game, Thomalla got a chance to come in. And in the modern world of college football, this was crucial exposure for Thomalla. He showed both Alabama, and the rest of the country, what he was capable of in a brief stint. Does that make him transfer-worthy? Or maybe more likely, does it make him backup-worthy if Mack chooses to transfer? Thomalla, with his play, made a positive statement. Jett Thomalla Stats Thomalla finished 3-for-5 passes for 36 yards and a touchdown. He also ran twice for 13 yards. Everything Thomalla did was a first for him at Alabama. It is time. Freshman Jett Thomalla, the No. 4 ranked quarterback in the 2026 class, will see his first game action in an Alabama uniform. Thomalla was the Gatorade & MaxPreps Nebraska Player of the Year. He is the state’s all-time leader in passing yards. — Brett Greenberg (@BrettGreenberg_) November 21, 2026 Sat down with Jett Thomalla well over a year ago after he flipped to Alabama. This kid said he wanted Bama bc he felt like the QBs there would force him to be a better player. Getting to see Jett out there today, looking VERY comfortable and confident, was an absolute treat. The future is very bright for this young man. — Waaaay Offsides Cotton (@AlafrigginBama) November 22, 2026 That included his first completion, an 11-yarder. The first snap of Alabama QB Jett Thomalla’s college career is an 11-yard completion to Derek Meadows. pic.twitter.com/MSSYNqIv8u — Theodore Fernandez (@TheoFernandez__) November 21, 2026 It also included his first touchdown pass, a nice dump-off to the running back Kevin Riley that he ran in for the score. Kevin Riley with his first TD of the season, and Jett Thomalla records his first TD pass of his career pic.twitter.com/HmlIHNHGsD — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 21, 2026 Jett Thomalla Future Thomalla would’ve realized in coming to Alabama that he may end up behind Russell for a couple seasons. Given that he stayed to this point, it seems likely he’ll remain for another year, potentially as the QB2 if Mack leaves. That would set up the talented Thomalla to start in 2028. If that’s what happens, it could end up being a great passing-of-the-torch from Russell to Thomalla. Saturday’s game doesn’t prove much, but i

item.title: Lionel Messi and Inter Miami humiliated as Columbus Crew cruise to dominant Game 1 playoff victory
item.description: FBL-MLS-INTER MIAMI-COLUMBUS CREW - AFP The dream of a back-to-back MLS Cup glory for Lionel Messi and Inter Miami is hanging by a thread following a disastrous 3-0 home defeat to the Columbus Crew. Despite entering the postseason as heavy favorites, the defending champions were dismantled in their first-ever playoff appearance at Nu Stadium on Saturday night. Self-inflicted errors spark Miami collapse Inter Miami fell behind after eight minutes when goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair rushed off his line and fouled Gonzalo Tapia in the box, allowing the forward to convert from the spot. Messi was then denied by a spectacular save from USMNT goalkeeper Patrick Schulte, while Luis Suarez poked wide with the goal at his mercy. St. Clair made smart stops to keep the deficit at 1-0, but defender Gonzalo Lujan collected two yellow cards for a 36th-minute red card before a frustrated Messi was booked for throwing the ball straight into Tapia's face from close range. Columbus punished the 10-man hosts with two goals in six early second-half minutes as Taha Habroune side-footed in Brais Méndez's through ball and Tapia turned Yannick Bright to race clear, allowing Crew interim coach Laurent Courtois to withdraw the striker with over 30 minutes left to preserve his legs and avoid a second booking. Gonzalez rues missed chances and turning point Inter Miami boss Kily Gonzalez blamed early missed opportunities and Lujan's dismissal for the defeat. "The team created four or five clear-cut chances to put the game away, but we couldn't convert, and their goalkeeper made the saves," Gonzalez told reporters. "Then came the red card, which completely changed the nature of the match. "But focusing on the 11 vs 11, we created plenty of chances; it was just one of those games where nothing goes your way, you just have to bite your tongue and endure it. There's still another leg to play - we have to go there, win and then come back and define it at home. I take full responsibility." Contrasting form exposes Miami's slump Second-seeded Miami, featuring Golden Boot winner and MVP favourite Messi, finished 13 points above seventh-seeded Columbus, yet have just five wins in their past 18 MLS matches and six in 17 at their new 26,700-seat Nu Stadium since April, failing to score there for the first time. Conversely, Courtois lifted the Crew from bottom of the Eastern Conference on September 1 on a league-best six-game winning streak. Brazilian midfielder Casemiro called for calm amid the elimination threat. "Pressure? Of course there is pressure," the former Real Madrid and Manchester United man said. "Inter Miami always plays to win and we know if we lose the next game we are out. So, that's the pressure. The most important thing now is to be calm. We know we have to do better, because we can do better. We were second on the table and so the next game we'll use it to show the rest how strong we are." item.title: 'Leave him alone' - Como boss Cesc Fabregas calls for Argentina to retire Lionel Messi's number 10 shirt to protect Nico Paz
item.description: Argentina v Costa Rica - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Como head coach Cesc Fabregas has urged the Argentina national team to retire Lionel Messi’s iconic number 10 jersey to shield Nico Paz from unfair expectations. The Spanish tactician believes that the young playmaker needs space to develop without the crushing weight of following in the footsteps of arguably the greatest player in history. Protecting the next generation The rise of Paz has sparked a significant debate regarding the future of the famous number 10 shirt for the Albiceleste . Following Messi's eventual departure from the international stage, many have pointed to the Como starlet as a natural successor . However, Fabregas has taken a firm stance against the idea, suggesting that the shirt should be permanently shelved out of respect for Messi and to protect the mental well-being of his young charge. He believes that placing such a historic burden on a developing player could be detrimental to their long-term growth. Fabregas is keen to ensure that the spotlight remains manageable for the 20-year-old, who has impressed in Serie A since his move from Real Madrid. The manager's comments underline a desire to avoid the "new Messi" tags that have hindered many young talents in the past. "Leave him alone. The number 10 is for Messi and that is it, it must be retired," the former Arsenal and Barcelona midfielder stated emphatically, as cited by TUTTOmercatoWEB . Managing international fatigue Beyond the symbolic weight of the jersey, Fabregas also addressed the physical toll that international duty takes on his squad. He noted that while representing one's country is a vital step for a player's career, it requires careful management upon their return to club football. The Como boss highlighted how Paz struggled physically after his initial call-up to the Argentina squad, appearing fatigued during a subsequent domestic fixture against Parma. "Yes, it helps that they go. Lucas [Da Cunha] is not too young, he is 25, but he has exploded very quickly. At the beginning, you struggle a bit. I remember Nico the first time in the national team, he came back and against Parma he was dead, he was walking on the pitch even though he had scored. You could see he wasn't himself. Now they manage themselves better," Fabregas said. Integration of rising stars The manager also touched upon the progress of Da Cunha and the workload of other squad members like Perrone. Da Cunha’s rapid rise to prominence has surprised even his manager, with the player recently receiving high praise from French legends. Fabregas is navigating the complexities of having players return from various parts of the globe, each with different levels of match fitness and emotional highs from their international exploits. item.title: Oregon Didn’t Play Saturday, But Ducks’ CFP Picture Changed Drastically
item.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 20: Dylan Raiola #8 of the Oregon Ducks celebrates his teammates second half touchdown run against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium on November 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) The Oregon Ducks didn’t have to play college football on Saturday. They had already taken the field on Friday night at Michigan State and pulled off a dominant victory. That meant they could just sit back and watch on Saturday as fires raged around their foes. Oregon’s College Football Playoff chances changed drastically on a day they didn’t even play. The Ducks entered the weekend ranked No. 13 in the CFP rankings. It’s a 12-team field, with the No. 12 spot likely going to the top Group of 6 finisher. That means Oregon needs to reach top-11 status to get into the dance. That’s a lot more likely after Saturday. Saturday Results Help Oregon Getty EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN – NOVEMBER 20: Dylan Raiola #8 of the Oregon Ducks celebrates his teammates second half touchdown run against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium on November 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Oregon essentially needed teams above it, or just below it, to start losing. Well, that happened. No. 4 UCLA lost to unranked Michigan. It seems like the Bruins should stay ahead of Oregon, as UCLA still has just one loss, but the gap has narrowed. No. 8 Indiana lost to Washington in overtime. It’s possible Oregon will leapfrog them in the rankings, too. And No. 14 Ohio State, trying to catch Oregon, lost to Nebraska. The Buckeyes’ CFP hopes are over. The chances are done for No. 16 Kentucky, too, which lost to Missouri. All four of those outcomes increase Oregon’s chances of being in the CFP field. They might even be a top-11 team in this week’s rankings before the final weekend of the regular season. item.title: Report – The real reason behind Ter Stegen’s recent visit to Barcelona training ground
item.description: Report – The real reason behind Ter Stegen’s recent visit to Barcelona training ground During the recent international break, former Barcelona captain Marc-Andre ter Stegen, currently on loan at AFC Ajax, paid a surprise visit to the club’s training facilities . After completing his national team duties with Germany, the 34-year-old flew to Catalonia and visited the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper , where he met and spoke with several of his former teammates. The truth behind Ter Stegen’s visit Now, according to SPORT , Ter Stegen’s visit to the Barcelona training facilities was primarily related to his ongoing knee rehabilitation. As per the report, the German international continues to receive treatment from the Blaugrana medical staff. Despite currently being away from the club on loan, the goalkeeper remains a Barcelona player. Ter Stegen recently visited the Barcelona training ground. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) The Catalans continue to monitor his physical condition, making regular contact with their medical department a natural part of the veteran star’s rehabilitation. As such, he returned to the city after completing his commitments with the German national team and spent several hours at the training ground as part of the continued monitoring of his knee. Barcelona retain an interest in Ter Stegen’s future Ter Stegen’s contractual situation means Barcelona will have to consider his future again once his loan spell at Ajax comes to an end. The German is currently playing for the Dutch club, but he expected to return to Barcelona after the loan. What happens next remains uncertain. One possibility is that he returns to see out his contract at the Spotify Camp Nou, which runs until June 2028. Another option is that he leaves permanently, with clubs like Valencia having shown interest. Ter Stegen’s contract at Barça runs until 2028. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) Ter Stegen’s performances in recent months with Ajax and Germany have reinforced his standing as a top goalkeeper with plenty left to offer. A regular for Ajax in goal, the 34-year-old shot-stopper has featured in 16 matches across all competitions for Michel’s side, keeping four clean sheets. Ter Stegen is also the No. 1 for the German national team under Jurgen Klopp, having had to play second-fiddle to the now-retired Manuel Neuer throughout his international career. With his contract expiring in 2028, he will be back at Barcelona once his loan spell at Ajax ends. Beyond that, his future remains uncertain.

item.title: Man United vs Bayern Munich: Massive update on Harry Kane’s participation in January CL tie
item.description: Man United vs Bayern Munich: Massive update on Harry Kane’s participation in January CL tie Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino agreed to take over at Old Trafford during the international break after the club parted ways with former manager Michael Carrick. The Englishman helped the Red Devils finish third in the Premier League last season and earned qualification to the Champions League. Unfortunately, he endured a difficult start to the campaign, managing just three wins in 15 games, including one in 10 games in the Premier League. With the team languishing in 18th place in the league, the English giants opted to part ways with Carrick and replaced him with Pochettino. The Argentine took charge earlier this week and is preparing to face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November. While Pochettino’s immediate responsibility will be dragging the club out of the relegation zone, he will also be tasked with earning qualification to the knockouts of the Champions League. The Red Devils have two wins and two defeats in Europe this season and are sitting in 17th place in the table. Their next fixture in the Champions League is against Sporting CP next week , although all eyes will be on the game against Bayern Munich at Old Trafford on 20 January. An update on the fixture has now emerged that could prove to be good news for the Red Devils. Kane set to miss United tie Bayern have confirmed that 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane will be sidelined for a while after suffering an ankle injury in the 1–1 draw with Koln on Friday. The report states : “Harry Kane tore his left ankle ligament in FC Bayern’s home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.” “This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern’s medical unit. It means the 33-year-old will be sidelined for the next few months.” The Bundesliga champions have since provided a fresh update on the Englishman’s situation, adding : “Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight after tearing his left ankle ligament in yesterday’s home match against 1. FC Köln. The 33-year-old will now begin his rehab.” Kane’s injury means that he is likely to miss out on a reunion with Pochettino, who transformed him into a potent goalscorer during their time together at Tottenham Hotspur. Kane remains on United’s radar United have long been linked with a move for Kane and missed out on the Englishman in the summer of 2023, before his move to the Allianz Arena. With neither Benjamin Sesko nor Joshua Zirkzee managing to impress so far, rumours of a return for Kane continue to circle. However, the move is likely to be very hard to materialise, especially given that the 33-year-old recently signed a new deal with the Bavarians. item.title: Video: ‘We love you’ – Fountain of Life Church members give Jimmy Odukoya rousing welcome
item.description: Members of the Fountain of Life Church have welcomed their senior pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, with cheers and chants of affection during Sunday service, days after a dispute over his leadership of the church became a subject of litigation. In a video from the service, Odukoya took the stage to applause from the congregation, who repeatedly chanted, “We love you.” 'We love you' — Fountain of Life Church members chant as Jimmy Odukoya takes the stage pic.twitter.com/YXNZljrfMv — TheCable (@thecableng) November 22, 2026 Responding to the reception, he said, “Fountain, I love you.” He added, “We have a lot to talk about, but first of all, we have a pleasant surprise this morning, Bishop Mike decided to surprise us this morning. Please welcome to the stage Bishop Mike Okonkwo.” The welcome came amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the church, which has seen rival positions emerge over Odukoya’s status as senior pastor. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect. The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023. The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration. item.title: School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school. Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building. The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him. Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen, said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound. Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba. He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped. The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building. “Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.” He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School. “Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.” When Vanguard visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off. The post School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
item.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. She stressed that teachers must possess the pedagogical skills to effectively reach all categories of learners and ensure inclusive classroom experiences. “This is why pedagogy is a critical component of our examination. “Without sound pedagogical skills, a person cannot b

item.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines. item.title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
item.description: Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state. Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy. The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident. According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy. Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded. He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents. The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State. He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations. Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss. item.title: Photos: Police take over Fountain of Life Church amid leadership crisis
item.description: …As trustees, Jimmy Odukoya trade court actions, church postpones thanksgiving service There was a heavy presence of police personnel at the headquarters of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday, as the leadership crisis rocking the church deepened, leaving worshippers uncertain about who would preside over the regular Sunday service. The security presence came amid a bitter dispute between Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and a group of church trustees over his continued leadership of the ministry founded by his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. The disagreement has escalated into a legal battle, with both sides seeking judicial intervention over the control and administration of the church. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted by Odukoya alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. The respondents include Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani, Pastor Akin Osinbajo, Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. In the court action, Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, as well as the decisions allegedly taken at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. How the crisis started The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as the senior pastor, with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and recorded succession instructions allegedly left by its late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, before his death in 2023. They maintained that the decision was intended to give effect to the founder’s wishes and ensure compliance with the church’s governing provisions. The group subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, the announcement immediately generated a counter-reaction from the church, which rejected the purported removal and described it as constitutionally invalid. In a statement issued after the announcement, the church maintained that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. It argued that his appointment in September 2023 was unanimously approved by the recognised board and that no constitutionally valid decision had been taken to remove him. item.title: PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday. Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+. The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. – ‘Not a problem’ – “This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.” Asked about the possibility of moving to sign a replacement in the January transfer window, the Spanish coach said PSG were “always open to possibilities”. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem,” he added. Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box. Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions. His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce. Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Lyon with Mads Bidstrup scoring the only goal. item.title: COP31 faces collapse threat as latest draft fails to mention fossil fuels
item.description: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks. The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy. The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations. The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia. An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal. “I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity. “The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas. Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise. The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly. And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. “We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices. “I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels. – Goal to electrify – The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”. The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. item.title: Kwara jailbreak: 20 officers queried as investigation reveals escape plans
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin About 20 officers of the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State, are being investigated over last Wednesday’s jailbreak by two condemned inmates. Vanguard reliably gathered that among those now facing scrutiny are members of the armed squad and duty officers on round-the-clock supervision of inmates at the facility. According to dependable sources (names withheld), probes indicate that last Wednesday’s jailbreak was a larger, coordinated effort involving seven inmates. According to insider accounts, the inmates spent months secretly chiseling through the wall of their cell without prison management detecting it, pasting a poster over the opening to conceal the gradual breach. On the morning of the escape, the convicts were said to have tied blankets to make a makeshift rope, throwing it to hook the broken bottles on the high perimeter fence. “While the first two convicts successfully scaled the wall and fled, the rope snapped under the weight of the remaining five inmates, sending them falling back,” the source hinted. Contacted,the Spokesperson of the state command, Adegbulugbe Phillips Olumide, however, could not confirm the development. “I cannot confirm the report; those who came to investigate the incident returned to Abuja yesterday,so there’s no report on the outcome yet.”he said Recall that the Controller General of Nigerian Correctional Service Sylvester Nwakuche,who visited the scene on Thursday, attributed the escape of two condemned prison inmates to negligence, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable. Nwakuche also vowed that staff found guilty in the incident would be dealt with severely. He, however, assured that a security dragnet has been spread across the state and the country and that the two escaped condemned criminals would be rearrested. Meanwhile, the inmates identified as Shegun and Abraham, who reportedly escaped on Wednesday after breaking and scaling the wall of the custodial centre to ease their escape, have been declared wanted by the centre. item.title: Messi deserved red card for throwing ball at opponent, says Columbus coach
item.description: Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday. Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time. Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card. “Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.” Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow. “The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter. Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia’s early penalty. Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami’s Nu Stadium. The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday. “It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. “We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added. “There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.” In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener. The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday. US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England’s 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia. Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring. New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday. Vanguard News The post Messi deserved red card for throwing ball at opponent, says Columbus coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation. The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts. In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel. She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities. According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee. A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects. The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 22 – Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 22 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . Juno continues in its looping elliptical orbit, swooping near the huge planet every 33 days and exploring a slightly different sector each time around. item.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
item.description: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. item.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations. It also emphasised the importance of enforcing safety measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents. ﻿ The post Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. This means the economic benefits are not confined to the railway operators. They extend to businesses, workers and communities along the routes. This is an important lesson i

item.title: Chelsea Humbled As Leeds Run Riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Leeds United’s English goalkeeper #01 James Trafford and Leeds United’s Swiss striker #19 Noah Okafor celebrate after the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in London on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
item.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

item.title: Amazon’s first digital photo frame is up to 50 percent off for Black Friday
item.description: Amazon only announced its first digital photo frame less than a month ago, but it’s already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. You can currently grab the Alexa Photo Frame at Amazon and Best Buy starting at $114 ($115 off), making it a great holiday gift for anyone who loves displaying family photos. If you prefer the walnut trim over the birch or standard black models, it’s also on sale at Best Buy for $134.99 ($95 off) — which, like with the others, is the first discount we’ve seen. Amazon Alexa Photo Frame Where to Buy: $229.99 $114.99 at Amazon (birch) $199.99 $114.99 at Best Buy (black) $229.99 $134.99 at Best Buy (walnut) The Alexa Photo Frame features a 10-inch, semi-matte touchscreen that’s designed to make digital photos look more natural, with built-in light sensors that automatically adjust brightness throughout the day. It displays images from Amazon Photos, which supports uploads from both iOS and Android devices, including photos stored in iCloud. You can choose which people or albums to display, or let Alexa Plus do the work, which often results in photos based on your facial expression, the season, and even the lighting. You can also search for specific photos with voice commands, letting you easily pull up images of your first dog, your child as a baby, and other shots without having to scroll endlessly through years of photos yourself. If you want to add a more personal touch, Amazon also lets you attach voice notes to individual photos via the Amazon Photos app. For example, you can add a recording of your kid explaining their Halloween costume to a trick-or-treating photo. Plus, you can preload the frame with photos and recordings before gifting it, so your loved one won’t have to spend time setting it up. We’re still testing Amazon’s answer to the Aura frame, but it looks like a particularly good option if you’re already an Amazon Prime member. A Prime subscription grants you unlimited full-resolution photo storage and access to Alexa Plus at no additional cost, and unlike Amazon’s smart displays, the frame doesn’t serve up annoying ads. That said, you don’t need a subscription to use it, and new users can always access a limited-time trial of Alexa Plus.

item.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. It's not quite "Khan", of course — what is? — but it deserves to be mentioned in the same breath. (Image credit: Paramount) In 1996, the "odd numbers bad, even num

item.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years. All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets. You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure , something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, on the Anthropic IPO and the economics of frontier AI. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Hayden Field, welcome back to Decoder . Thanks. Great to be here. I’m excited to talk to you today because it’s not pure soap opera drama chaos. I know. It’s like a normal thing that happened. It’s for once not personality-based and soap opera. It’s about cold, hard would-be cash. [Laughs] Well, there is some personality in it because we’re going to talk a lot about Anthropic’s IPO, which has a bunch of big personalities in it, and the way they have structured this company to repel the rapacious pressures of capitalism is, I would say, very eccentric. It reflects the beliefs of a number of eccentric people. Yep, absolutely. It’s really been interesting digging into the S-1 again and just seeing who was on what committee and which founders have the most control here and how much control the founders actually have, which is more than it may seem. Let’s start at the start. You and I are talking on IPO day. Anthropic is the first pure AI lab to go public. They priced the IPO at $83 a share and they got all the way up to $111. By the time people are listening to this, who knows what the price will actually be, but it’s been a real victory lap for all the people who are invested in Anthropic. A bunch of law firms have changed their homepages to be like, “Congratulations, guys!” What do yo

item.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
item.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that . Assembly of that new Starlink network is already underway. Ship carried 26 of the next-gen internet spacecraft up for the first time on F

item.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
item.description: At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. His son, Donald Trump Jr, made a similar statement about Haitian people in 2024 (Trump’s government has since ended the protected status of both Somali and Haitian migrants in the US). These statements and their consequences are symptoms of a growing trend in Western politics: the re-emergence of racial views of human nature that have been largely in hiding for the past 70 years. Narratives about the innate intellectual inferiority of black or brown people compared with white people—which can still be found in academic journals today—are fuelling far-right propaganda in some of the world’s largest democracies. Such claims underpin misinformation strategies on social media and bolster political movements. These narratives are sometimes euphemistically referred to as “ race science ” or more recently “race realism.” But, as we argue, they are not actually scientific. One member of this community, Nathan Cofnas , recently attracted public attention by accusing the late Jason Arday of plagiarism. Read full article Comments

item.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
item.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.
